obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities must annually report to the Commission and relevant national competition authorities any information from market surveillance activities that may be of potential interest for the application of Union competition law, and must also annually report on prohibited practices and measures taken.

Member States must designate the authority responsible for market surveillance under Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I Section A as the market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems related to products covered by that legislation.
exceptions: Member States may designate another relevant authority in appropriate circumstances, provided coordination with relevant sectoral market surveillance authorities is ensured.

obligations.summary: For high-risk AI systems placed on the market, put into service, or used by regulated financial institutions, Member States must designate the relevant national financial supervisory authority as the market surveillance authority where the AI system is in direct connection with the provision of financial services.
exceptions: In appropriate circumstances, and provided coordination is ensured, Member States may designate another relevant authority as market surveillance authority.

obligations.summary: National market surveillance authorities supervising regulated credit institutions participating in the Single Supervisory Mechanism must report without delay to the European Central Bank any information from market surveillance activities that may be of potential interest for the ECB's prudential supervisory tasks.

Member States must designate competent data protection supervisory authorities or equivalent authorities as market surveillance authorities for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III point 1 used for law enforcement, border management, justice and democracy purposes, and for systems listed in Annex III points 6, 7, and 8.
exceptions: Market surveillance activities shall not affect the independence of judicial authorities or interfere with their activities when acting in a judicial capacity.

obligations.summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor must act as market surveillance authority for Union institutions, bodies, offices, or agencies that fall within the scope of this Regulation.
exceptions: Does not apply to the Court of Justice of the European Union acting in its judicial capacity.

obligations.summary: Member States must facilitate coordination between market surveillance authorities designated under this Regulation and other relevant national authorities or bodies supervising the application of Union harmonisation legislation or other Union law relevant to high-risk AI systems in Annex III.

Providers must grant market surveillance authorities full access to documentation as well as training, validation, and testing datasets used for the development of high-risk AI systems, including through APIs or other technical means enabling remote access where appropriate.
exceptions: Access is subject to security safeguards where appropriate.

obligations.summary: Providers must grant market surveillance authorities access to the source code of high-risk AI systems upon a reasoned request when access is necessary to assess conformity and testing or auditing based on provided data and documentation has been exhausted or proved insufficient.
exceptions: Access is only required when both conditions are fulfilled: (a) access is necessary to assess conformity with Chapter III Section 2 requirements, and (b) testing or auditing based on provider-supplied data and documentation has been exhausted or proved insufficient.

obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities must treat any information or documentation obtained in the exercise of their tasks in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78.
